correctness.rationale: With signed masses w_i on the m strictly ordered nonzero magnitudes a_i, the bias equals sum_i w_i min(a_i,c). Mean zero sets its right tail to zero and b(0)=0. Every nonzero sign component must contain a nonzero interior knot because no affine piece with two zero endpoints can be nonzero. Thus the m−1 potential knot components allow at most m−2 reversals, including in the presence of vanishing signed masses or zero intervals. For the proposed alternating unit-height knot pattern on 1,…,m−1 and zero endpoint values, negative jumps of slope have absolute magnitudes 3, then 4 at each interior index up through m−2, then 3 and 1; these sum to 4m−5. Telescoping gives zero first moment and interpolated biases of alternating height ±1/(4m−5), so the simple half-integer crossings are exactly as stated. For this family only, two roots of the nondecreasing drift would imply each positively weighted score is constant on their interval and hence saturated; zero total would require a subset of weight exactly one half, impossible for the odd denominator. The root sign is opposite the drift at zero. Monotonicity and unit Lipschitz constant give (x−x_c)F_c(x)≥F_c(x)^2 and hence the residual decrease eta(2−eta)F_c(x)^2 in squared distance; boundedness and uniqueness give global convergence at each fixed c. This is deterministic population convergence, not stochastic sample-path convergence. Inspected the frozen verifier without running it; its exact finite cap tests do not establish the general bound or uniqueness.

Qian et al. give a direction error for three component gradients at one point and one cap.

The proof needs both spline endpoint cancellation and conversion of arbitrary alternating knot data into a centered, positive-weight, non-half-partition law, rather than transferring an earlier fixed-cap example or convergence result.

evidence: The drift zero is exactly the Huber location score equation after the sign change in location, with weights fixed as c varies; a count of the signs attained by this score at the mean is an equivalent test.

As a spline in c, the claim is a zero-boundary interpolation bound with one-sided truncated linear basis min(a_i,c), not the Resultary spline L² projection's total-variation norm inequality. The Huber article's full text was not independently obtained.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalence would make any prior sharp fixed-law Huber path crossing theorem covering. Classical location-score equivalence by itself does not give the endpoint count with realizable probability weights and unique roots.

value.rationale: The result addresses a specific obstruction to interpreting bias bounds: increasing the cap can repeatedly move the population equilibrium from one side of the true minimizer to the other for one unchanged law. The exact minimum noise complexity, an explicit rational family for each feasible count, and uniqueness and convergence over that family make the boundary sharp and meaningful. It is not a statement about privacy or sampled SGD.
